title: YOU DON'T NEED GAP INSURANCE ON YOUR CAR: Find out WHY - Auto Expert: The Homework Guy, Kevin Hunter
summary: The Homework Guy argues GAP insurance is oversold at the dealer finance office and explains how to avoid ever needing it.

assertions.quote: it covers the difference between the actual cash value of your car and that whopping big fat loan balance

verdicts.note: Clearly defined by the FTC and insurers; it does not cover mechanical repairs at all.

assertions.quote: car dealers charged customers like mr. Dover between 500 and $1,000 for their gap policy

verdicts.note: Matches the broader documented pattern of F&I add-on markups.
NCLC's executive summary: "add-on products are sold at prices far higher than dealer cost, marked up by a far higher percentage than dealers mark up the cars themselves."

assertions.quote: negative equity means the loan balance is higher than the actual cash value

verdicts.note: A direct, verifiable consequence of how GAP coverage is defined.

CFPB found a GAP shortfall is more likely on a high-LTV loan than a low-LTV one; negative equity rolled into a new loan raises LTV, but the document discusses LTV generally, not negative equity specifically.

assertions.quote: if you're a smart car buyer you always put 20% more cash down

verdicts.note: A larger down payment directly narrows or eliminates the loan-to-value gap GAP insurance covers.

CFPB's derived comparison states a larger down payment (lower LTV) reduces the benefit a GAP product provides, since a low-LTV loan's insurer payout on a totaled vehicle may already cover the remaining debt.
